overview: The committee discussed proposed zoning boundary changes for the Boston Avenue corridor and reviewed building non-conformity data. Members provided guidance on including specific parcels, such as St. Clement’s Church, and discussed the timeline for the forthcoming Tufts Institutional Zone proposal.

items.title: Boston Avenue Corridor Zoning Presentation
items.summary: Emily Innes presented non-conformity studies for the northern and southern sections of the Boston Avenue corridor, showing that most existing lots fail current standards for frontage, setbacks, and lot size. The presentation illustrated how current zoning creates barriers to reinvestment in established neighborhoods.

items.title: Boundary Guidance and District Standards
items.summary: The committee provided direction to include Apartment 1 districts and specific commercial nodes within the northwestern boundary to better reflect existing mixed-use patterns. Members also discussed adopting structural cleanup items used in the Medford Square zoning, such as standardized footnotes and separated waiver sections.

items.title: Student Housing and Light Industrial Uses
items.summary: Councilors discussed creating specific definitions for private, taxable student housing in O2 zones to address local housing shortages and the potential for 'maker spaces' to support small entrepreneurs. Director Hunt noted complications regarding inclusionary housing and parking requirements for student-focused developments.

items.title: South Boston Avenue and St. Clement's Parcels
items.summary: The committee reached a consensus to expand the southern boundary to include the St. Clement’s Church and school properties to incentivize mixed-use redevelopment rather than pure residential use. The boundary was also adjusted to include specific Tufts-owned parcels that face residential neighborhoods along Boston Avenue.

items.title: Public Comment and Tufts Institutional Zone Timeline
items.summary: Residents questioned the rationale for boundary selections and requested transparency regarding internal meetings between the city and Tufts University. Chair Leming clarified that a list of bulleted concerns from Tufts would be made public and that a draft of the institutional zone proposal is expected for the May 5th meeting.

items.title: Conclusion and Adjournment
items.summary: The committee voted to keep the matter in committee and adjourned.
